page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m2.large is a burstable instance type belonging to the ecs.t6 family. It is equipped with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon 8269CY core running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps under a KVM hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned at the lower tier of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1300.19, and the multi-core score is 2402.69, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show a sharp drop-off from 186.46 GB/sec for small cached blocks down to 20.68 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, which is categorized in the bottom 10%. Geekbench scores further reflect these limitations, with a single-core score of 1045.0 and a multi-core score of 1850.0.

Due to its burstable CPU allocation model, the instance is designed for workloads with low baseline CPU utilization that experience occasional spikes. This resource-sharing model makes it a highly cost-efficient option for entry-level tasks, but it presents a clear tradeoff in sustained performance. Benchmark results for application workloads, such as Redis SET operations at 2.57 million operations per second and static web serving at 2.44 GB/sec, confirm its suitability is restricted to lightweight applications. Appropriate workloads include microservices, development or testing environments, low-traffic web servers, and basic administrative tasks.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance utilizes a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU resources. Benchmark evaluations place its performance in the lower tier, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 2402.69 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1850.0. It is best suited for low-traffic web serving, development and testing environments, and lightweight background tasks.
